brief: NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on 23 November, eleven days after the board had unanimously accepted his resignation and said on the 17 November earnings call it would not bring him back. The reversal followed reported comments from President Trump, who said he personally spoke with the board, and the board cited US government input in concluding Huang's return poses no national security risk, though its own investigation into a reported foreign-intelligence targeting of Huang and an SEC review of NVIDIA's disclosures remain open. Shares, down 23% the prior week (worst since October 2008) and 47.5% off their 6 October high, rose 31.48% to USD 165.05 on the news, back above the USD 164 support broken the week before, while the forward multiple rebounded to about 11x from an 8.2x low. Because NVIDIA is about 7% of the SOX and Nasdaq 100, the swing dragged the broader AI trade down and back up with it. Separately, Q3 revenue grew 103% y/y and beat consensus, while free cash flow of USD 43.8bn missed by 23% as receivables jumped from USD 63bn to USD 81bn. Syz says key-man risk persists and recommends a barbell between AI exposure and defensives.
